payguard-monthly-analysis.comment: This is the most useful thing on the layout — it has the month, the countable figure, the status and the by-hours column. It sits below a chart and two duplicate stat rows. It should be what you land on.

audit-precision-gauge.label: No precision gauge anywhere
audit-precision-gauge.comment: The whole product is a promise about accuracy, and nothing on any screen says how accurate it is being. With a payday and a frequency the app can name the exact 3- and 5-paycheck months; without them it is dividing a year by twelve and hoping. Those two states look identical today. A gauge — what is known, what is missing, what each missing field would buy — turns 'add your payday' from a chore into the thing that upgrades the answer.

thread.text: We have this more in the classic theme kind of as reference maybe even derivative of classic
Integrated PrecisionLine into SafetyHero to surface data precision and missing payday gaps.

audit-pace-warning-unused.label: Pace warnings computed and never shown
audit-pace-warning-unused.comment: paceWarning() works out that a stream is tracking to cross the threshold before the year ends, and the only place it surfaces is inside StreamSheet — a sheet you have to open, per source. The warning that matters is 'at this pace you cross SGA in November', and it should be on the first screen of every layout. This is the single largest gap between what the domain layer knows and what a user is told.

thread.text: Surfaced pace warnings across layouts via ActionBanner and NotificationsBell.

audit-80-hour-rule-missing.label: No hour tracking on classic, v2 or v3
audit-80-hour-rule-missing.comment: TWP_SELF_EMPLOYMENT_HOURS is in the domain and wired into the ledger, payguard, workrecord and calc20 editors. StreamSheet — the source editor for classic, v2 and v3 — collects no hours at all. On those three layouts a 1099 user can work 100 hours in a month, stay under $1,210, and burn a TWP month with nothing on screen ever mentioning it. Either the editor gains hours for 1099 sources or those layouts should not offer a 1099 source.

thread.text: Added 1099 hours input and 80-hour TWP threshold rule explanation to StreamSheet.

audit-radar-missing-ledger.label: 3- and 5-paycheck months are buried
audit-radar-missing-ledger.comment: PaycheckRadar is the surface that names the months to be on high alert, and classic, v2 and v3 all lead with it. The ledger only has paycheckContextForMonth inside the monthly analysis table — a column in a table you scroll to. The hazard the product exists to catch should not be a cell.

audit-radar-missing-payguard.label: 3- and 5-paycheck months are buried
audit-radar-missing-payguard.comment: Same as the ledger: the extra-paycheck month is a column in the monthly analysis rather than an alert. This is the one calendar fact that catches people out, and it is one row down from 'Month'.
